Featured investigation

Historical Mystery No. 1: Kennedy

Sixty years on, the assassination of President John F. Kennedy remains the most examined — and most argued-over — event in modern history. We rebuilt Dealey Plaza in 3D, compiled the archives, and laid out the evidence. The question at the centre of it all: who really fired the shots?

Enter the Kennedy Archive About our mission
About us

History you don't just learn — you step inside it.

History Time Machine SI creates content and technology that allows people to step back in time: to witness historical events, explore historical locations, meet historical figures, and learn history in real time, within real places.

Our Mission

To make history tangible. We rebuild the places and moments that shaped our world as interactive 3D experiences and films — researched from primary sources, measured against the real ground, and open to everyone — so the past can be witnessed, questioned and understood first-hand rather than taken on trust.

Our Vision

A complete time machine: every era of human history — from the first stone tools to the Space Age — rebuilt as a place you can visit. A library of living history where a student, a researcher or the simply curious can stand where history happened and watch it unfold around them.

How We Work

Every recreation starts in the archive: official records, original film, photographs, surveys and testimony. We build to that evidence, label what is documented and what is debated, and show our sources — because an honest reconstruction is worth more than a dramatic one.

Our values

  • Evidence first. Primary sources — records, film, surveys, testimony — drive every model, script and claim we publish.
  • Honest about uncertainty. Where the record is disputed, we say so on screen and show the competing accounts side by side.
  • Accuracy over spectacle. Measured distances, real timelines and named sources — never drama dressed up as fact.
  • Access for everyone. History belongs to everybody; our experiences are built to be explored by any curious mind.
  • Respect for the real people. These events happened to real lives. We treat victims, witnesses and families with care.
  • Always building. The archive never closes — every project adds models, films and research for the next journey.

Historical Mysteries · No. 1

Kennedy: Who really fired the shots?

On November 22, 1963, President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dealey Plaza, Dallas. The official investigations, the surviving film and six decades of argument have never fully settled the central mystery — how many shooters were there, and where were they standing? This is our investigation headquarters: the story, the evidence, the archives, the film, and the interactive 3D model.

Open the 3D Model Browse the Archives

The assassination — November 22, 1963

11:40 AM — Air Force One lands

President and Mrs. Kennedy arrive at Dallas Love Field and join Governor John Connally and his wife Nellie in the open presidential limousine for the motorcade through downtown Dallas.

12:29 PM — The motorcade turns onto Elm Street

The limousine turns left from Houston Street onto Elm Street, passing the Texas School Book Depository and slowing toward the triple underpass, in front of the grassy knoll.

12:30 PM — Shots in Dealey Plaza

Gunfire. President Kennedy and Governor Connally are both wounded. Abraham Zapruder, filming from a concrete pedestal beside Elm Street, captures the sequence on 8mm film — 486 frames that became the most studied footage in history. The final, fatal shot strikes the President as the limousine passes the grassy knoll.

1:00 PM — The President is declared dead

At Parkland Memorial Hospital, John F. Kennedy is pronounced dead. Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson is sworn in aboard Air Force One later that afternoon.

1:15 PM — Officer J.D. Tippit is murdered

Dallas police officer J.D. Tippit is shot in the Oak Cliff neighbourhood. Lee Harvey Oswald is arrested in the Texas Theatre nearby shortly afterwards and charged with both murders.

November 24 — Oswald is shot on live television

Two days later, nightclub owner Jack Ruby shoots Oswald in the basement of Dallas police headquarters, live on national television — silencing the accused assassin before any trial, and guaranteeing the questions would never close.

The mystery: who was the shooter?

Two official investigations reached two different conclusions — and the argument between them is the mystery.

Warren Commission · 1964

One gunman, behind the motorcade

The Warren Commission concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone, firing three shots from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository. Its most debated finding — the "single bullet theory" — holds that one bullet passed through President Kennedy and then Governor Connally, accounting for both men's non-fatal wounds so the timing of the shots fits Oswald's rifle.

House Select Committee · 1979

A probable conspiracy

The House Select Committee on Assassinations agreed Oswald fired the shots that killed the President — but concluded Kennedy "was probably assassinated as a result of a conspiracy," based largely on acoustic evidence suggesting a fourth shot from the grassy knoll, in front of the limousine. That acoustics finding was later challenged, and the debate it opened has never been settled.

The Zapruder film

Frame 313 records the fatal shot. Supporters of the official account read the President's movements as consistent with a shot from behind; critics point to the backward motion of his head as evidence of a shot from the front — the grassy knoll. The film is the centre of the argument precisely because both sides claim it.

The grassy knoll

Dozens of witnesses reported shots, smoke or a gunman from the knoll and its wooden fence. No shooter was ever found there, and the physical evidence is contested to this day — which is why our model lets you stand at the fence and judge the sightlines yourself.

Oswald — and Ruby

Oswald denied everything — "I'm just a patsy" — and was murdered before he could be tried. Whether he was a lone malcontent, one shooter among several, or exactly what he claimed to be remains the open core of the case.

Our approach: the evidence is presented as it stands — documented fact labelled as documented, disputed claims labelled as disputed — and the 3D model is built so you can test the sightlines, distances and timings for yourself.

The 3D interactive model & the film

Our cinematic reconstruction rebuilds the entire Dealey Plaza event in 3D: real footage — news broadcasts, the Zapruder film and other home movies — dropped into the rebuilt plaza at its original camera positions, narrated by a deep, calm documentary voice. The model underneath the film is the same one you can explore yourself.
